messages:
alex_support: opening escalation for ticket #78990 — ACME reports large latency and auth 401 spike for EU users around 11:40-12:10 CET, plus duplicate billing events after retries. They saw many clients routed to APAC IPs. Need quick triage. :mega:

marta_prod: saw customer logs — lots of frontend preconnects and service-worker fetches showing an A record for api.redwood.ai pointing to 13.250.11.9 (ap-southeast). Origin remains in eu-west but clients hit apac, RTT goes +220ms and requests retry.

rick_net: ran a probe from our AMS probe and a TeleNord-resolver (customer ISP) capture. Looks like EDNS client subnet is being stripped by upstream resolver and a cached global anycast answer returns ap-southeast. Suspect stale geoip DB or resolver cache poisoning.

marta_prod: customer provided this dig output from their TeleNord gateway (DE):
```
$ dig @194.168.4.1 +short api.redwood.ai
13.250.11.9
$ dig @194.168.4.1 api.redwood.ai +noall +answer
api.redwood.ai. 3600 IN A 13.250.11.9
```
TTL 3600 is long — if preconnects pin that, clients keep hitting wrong region for an hour.

rick_net: repro steps for eng oncall:
1) from an EU VM, run `dig @194.168.4.1 +edns=0 api.redwood.ai` and `dig @8.8.8.8 +edns=1 api.redwood.ai` to compare ECS behavior
2) `curl -v --resolve api.redwood.ai:443:13.250.11.9 https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health` to reproduce higher latency + auth timeouts
3) capture tcpdump to confirm source IP mapping

ops-bot: alert: cross-region egress spike detected — eu-pop -> apac-pop increased by ~900 rps between 11:38-12:12 CET; auth 401 rate +180% (11:40-12:15).

maya_billing: customers complained of duplicate invoice line items due to retries hitting billing endpoint twice. I'll start a provisional credit plan. Proposing 15% credit for affected window unless SRE recommends more.

jules_sre: quick hypothesis: chain is (1) resolver returns old/stale anycast IP that points to apac because of cached mapping in some resolvers; (2) browsers/service-workers prefetch that address and keep it in cache; (3) traffic goes to apac, auth tokens TTL or idempotency assumptions fail and retries hit billing path twice. Also some resolvers may be doing EDNS stripping causing wrong geo answers.

alex_support: customer also says they use a heavy preconnect strategy in their SPA (prefetch + preconnect on app load) — that amplifies damage if DNS answer is wrong. Asked them to disable preconnect temporarily.

rick_net: vendor/partner checklist to open with our DNS/CDN providers:
- verify if any resolver upstream is stripping ECS/EDNS and returning a global anycast IP
- check GeoIP DB consistency across POPs and any stale host-to-region mappings
- investigate if our DNS cache warmer or prefetchers accidentally primed wrong region IPs to some resolvers
Include dig outputs and timestamps.

jules_sre: I'm opening vendor ticket now and attaching our packet captures + dig traces. Also adding a temporary routing soft-affinity rule so that when RTT diff < 120ms we prefer same-region replicas to avoid immediate cross-region fallbacks while vendor investigates.

marta_prod: short-term mitigations proposed:
- Lower authoritative TTL on edge A records to 60s for EU set for next 6 hours (owner: dns-team)
- Routing soft-affinity (owner: routing-team) for 4h window
- Ask affected customers to clear service-worker caches / remove hard-coded DNS entries (owner: customer success)
- Issue provisional credits (owner: maya_billing)

maya_billing: drafting credits. Holding until SRE confirms exact windows. Will message ACME with apology + credit estimate. :pray:

jules_sre: action items and ETAs:
- jules_sre: vendor ticket + attach traces/dig (ETA 1h)
- rick_net: collect 3 ISP dig outputs from customer-provided probes (ETA 45m)
- dns-team: lower TTL (ETA 30m) — requires risk check for failovers
- routing-team: deploy soft-affinity rule (ETA 1h)
- maya_billing: prepare credit communication (ETA 2h)

alex_support: noted. I've told ACME CS to pause aggressive prefetch and to collect additional sysproxy/resolver dig outputs.

marta_prod: logging tip for oncall: check auth node logs for token validation latency and ip of client seen by auth service — if client_ip is in apac range during window, confirms misroute.

jules_sre: will post vendor response here once available. thanks team. :white_check_mark:
